POSITIVE_CONTROL_SYNTHETIC_SPA.description: 8-state synthetic deterministic SPA with known beyond-Markov structure, N=5000, K=3

NULL_CONTROL_WITHIN_STRATUM_PERMUTATION.description: Within-stratum conditional permutation: shuffle url_after within each (url_before, history) stratum, 1000 perms, seed=42. Expected mean PMI ~0 bits.
NULL_CONTROL_WITHIN_STRATUM_PERMUTATION.interpretation: Within-stratum permutation reduces null mean from 0.552 (block) to 0.417, a 24.4% improvement, but still fails to center null at zero. The residual bias of 0.417 bits indicates that within-stratum shuffling does not fully eliminate the action-PMI coupling. Deterministic strata (31.5%) contribute PMI=0 by construction but do not offset the stochastic strata bias.

NULL_CONTROL_BLOCK_PERMUTATION_DIAGNOSTI.description: Trajectory-level block permutation (parent method, known biased). Diagnostic comparison.
NULL_CONTROL_BLOCK_PERMUTATION_DIAGNOSTI.interpretation: Replicates parent null bias exactly (0.552). Confirms the bias is intrinsic to hash-routed SPA, not specific to permutation method.

NULL_CONTROL_ACTION_SHUFFLE_DIAGNOSTIC.description: Action-shuffle diagnostic: shuffle action labels within each trajectory.
NULL_CONTROL_ACTION_SHUFFLE_DIAGNOSTIC.interpretation: Action-shuffle yields null mean 0.406, very close to within-stratum 0.417. This convergence suggests the bias is a property of the estimator weighting across deterministic/stochastic strata, not the specific permutation scheme.

observations: 5000 transitions collected in-memory from 12-state SPA simulation: 50 sessions x 100 steps, seed=42, same SHA256(prev1:prev2:current:action) transition function as parent EXP-PHYSICS-35375596894. Raw SHA256 170df6e34c78f64584f5332d61b9a705d87838b61e24eb04bdd4cc1b095c6ade (matches parent exactly, confirming identical data).

Within-stratum conditional permutation null mean at K=2 = 0.417 bits. This FAILS the frozen primary falsifier (|mean| < 0.1 bits). The null is biased high by 0.417 bits, resolving 24.4% of the inherited C4 bias (parent block perm mean 0.552) but remaining 4.17x above the threshold.

Action-shuffle diagnostic yields null mean 0.406 bits, nearly identical to within-stratum (0.417). This convergence strongly suggests the bias is an intrinsic property of the PMI estimator weighting across deterministic/stochastic strata, not specific to the permutation scheme. When 31.5% of strata are deterministic (PMI=0), the weighted average is dominated by stochastic strata where any non-randomization of the true action-outcome coupling inflates the null.

Block permutation null mean 0.552 bits replicates parent exactly, confirming measurement reproducibility. All three permutation methods fail to center null at zero, with action-shuffle (0.406) and within-stratum (0.417) converging near each other, well above the 0.1 threshold.

PMI signal remains strong and reproducible: state K2 PMI = 0.933 bits (p=0.001, d=79.7), unconditional K0 = 1.419 bits, K1 = 1.531 bits, action K3 = 1.221 bits. All match parent within floating-point precision, confirming the PMI pipeline is deterministic and reproducible.
Positive control passes strongly: 8-state deterministic SPA state K3 PMI = 1.671 bits, action K3 = 1.806 bits, both p=0.001. Pipeline validated at N=5000.

Phase 2 (production SPA testing) was not attempted because Phase 1 falsified: the null control methodology does not center null at zero for hash-routed SPAs, so any production SPA result would be uninterpretable under the invalidated measurement framework.

Determinism check K2: 885/1292 stochastic (68.5%), 407 deterministic (31.5%). The deterministic strata contribute PMI=0 by construction and dilute the weighted average. The stochastic strata carry the signal but also the null bias.
validity_notes: Within-stratum conditional permutation was the hypothesized fix for the inherited C4 failure. The analytic argument (preserves P(url_after|stratum) while breaking I(url_after; action|stratum), E[PMI]=0) is sound for infinite samples. The finite-sample bias (0.417 bits) indicates that either (a) the strata are too small for the analytic expectation to hold, or (b) the deterministic/stochastic stratum mixing creates a weighted-average bias that cannot be eliminated by any permutation scheme that preserves marginal stratum distributions.

The convergence of within-stratum (0.417) and action-shuffle (0.406) null means suggests the bias floor is ~0.41 bits for this SPA design at N=5000. This is an intrinsic property of the PMI estimator on this environment, not a fixable permutation artifact.

Block permutation bias (0.552) is 25% higher than within-stratum (0.417), confirming that trajectory-level block shuffling introduces additional artificial state-history correlation beyond the intrinsic estimator bias. The within-stratum method partially addresses this but does not eliminate it.

The experiment is COMPLETE (measurement valid) but FALSIFIES the null centering hypothesis. This is a valid scientific negative: the revised null control methodology does not resolve C4 for hash-routed SPAs.

Playwright browser automation not available in CI (chromium_headless_shell-1243 missing). HTTP API diagnostic validated server logic. Phase 2 production SPA testing was precluded by Phase 1 falsification, not infrastructure.

No Bonferroni correction needed for primary C4 test (single comparison). The within-stratum p=0.001 confirms observed PMI is significantly above the biased null, but the biased null itself fails the centering criterion.
unresolved: Why does within-stratum conditional permutation fail to center null at zero? The analytic argument (E[PMI]=0 under independence within strata) should hold for sufficiently large strata. Possible explanations: (a) stratum sizes are too small (mean 2.89 obs/stratum at K2, 398 used of 1292); (b) deterministic strata (31.5%) with PMI=0 create a floor that inflates the weighted average when stochastic strata are biased; (c) the PMI estimator (log2 of ratio) has finite-sample bias that is not centered by permutation.

Is the 0.417-bit null bias reducible by alternative methods? Candidate approaches: (a) model-based null (parametric bootstrap from estimated transition probabilities); (b) stratified permutation with minimum stratum size >5; (c) unbiased PMI estimator (Miller-Madow correction); (d) conditional entropy H(url_after|action,url_before,history) as alternative to PMI.

Does the convergence of within-stratum and action-shuffle null means (0.417 vs 0.406) imply a fundamental limit for this estimator class? If so, the 0.933-bit observed PMI may be interpretable as signal minus bias (~0.52 bits true signal), but this requires independent validation.

Whether the null bias is specific to hash-routed SPA with SHA256 transition function, or generalizes to other deterministic/stochastic SPA designs. The bias floor of ~0.41 bits at N=5000 may vary with SPA cardinality, stratum dimensionality, and transition function properties.

Phase 2 production SPA testing remains untested. The validated PMI pipeline (0.933 bits, p=0.001) detects signal but without a valid null control, the p-value and significance claims cannot be confirmed. A different falsification framework is needed before production testing is meaningful.
